content.value_statement: Long project instructions can hide important guidance and verification steps. This skill restructures them into concise root guidance and focused rule files.
actual_capabilities: Reports whether a CLAUDE.md file is within the recommended length range.
Suggests concise root guidance and linked .claude/rules files.
Finds project test, lint, typecheck, and build commands for verification guidance.
Identifies conflicting instructions and asks the user to choose a version.
Suggests reusable global-skill candidates when instructions apply across projects.
Flags redundant, vague, or inferable content for removal.
limitations: It does not automatically resolve conflicting instructions without user input.
It can only discover commands and files available in the current project.
Suggested rule organization requires review for project-specific accuracy.
It does not replace team documentation or repository maintenance policies.

use_cases.title: Simplify repository guidance
use_cases.description: Turn an oversized CLAUDE.md into a concise entry point with focused linked rules.

use_cases.title: Add reliable verification steps
use_cases.description: Discover available project commands and document checks after code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare reusable instructions
use_cases.description: Identify framework guidance that may be better maintained as a global Claude skill.

prompt_templates.title: Review my CLAUDE.md
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CLAUDE.md for length, clarity, and missing verification guidance. Suggest a concise structure before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor project instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this repository CLAUDE.md using progressive disclosure. Keep project-specific commands at the root and move detailed rules into .claude/rules.

prompt_templates.title: Find instruction conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my CLAUDE.md and related rule files for conflicting instructions. List each conflict and ask me which instruction to retain.

prompt_templates.title: Create a verification plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project configuration and propose a CLAUDE.md verification section. Include only discovered test, lint, typecheck, and build commands.

output_examples.input: Refactor a 160-line CLAUDE.md for a TypeScript service.
output: Reports that the file needs refactoring.
Keeps project commands and verification steps at the root.
Proposes separate rule files for testing and TypeScript conventions.

output_examples.input: Check a repository for missing verification guidance.
output: Finds available package scripts and task runners.
Suggests a Verification section with relevant commands.
Explains which commands should remain documented.

best_practices: Review proposed file moves before applying them.
Keep only project-specific guidance in the root CLAUDE.md.
Run documented verification commands after every meaningful change.
anti_patterns: Do not copy global workflow instructions without adapting them to the project.
Do not keep duplicated guidance in both CLAUDE.md and rule files.
Do not document commands that the project does not support.

faq.question: What does progressive disclosure mean?
faq.answer: It keeps essential project guidance in CLAUDE.md and moves detailed guidance into linked rule files.

faq.question: Does this skill edit files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a structured refactoring workflow. Review proposed changes before applying them.

faq.question: Can it find test commands?
faq.answer: It checks common project configuration and task-runner files for available verification commands.

faq.question: How short should CLAUDE.md be?
faq.answer: The skill treats fewer than 50 lines as ideal and 50 to 100 lines as acceptable.

faq.question: Can it resolve conflicting team policies?
faq.answer: No. It identifies conflicts and asks you which policy should remain.

faq.question: When should I create a global skill?
faq.answer: Create one when substantial guidance applies to multiple projects and is not project-specific.
